title: Laplacian and sensitivity
statement: For a Boolean function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ and an input $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$, the cube Laplacian of the real-valued version of $f$ at $x$ equals that value times the number of coordinates whose flip changes $f(x)$; that is, $\Delta f(x)=f(x)\,\mathrm{sensitivity}(f,x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$x$ is an input in the sign cube
